description: §23.5.4 — closest-ancestor-wins, NO union. The OUTER `<program>` declares `capabilities=[network("api.example.com")]`; the INNER `<program name="svc">` declares an explicit `capabilities=[]`. The `use foreign:svc` construct inside the inner program is governed by the INNER's set (the CLOSEST ancestor with `capabilities=`), which is EMPTY — it does NOT union with the outer network. So W-FOREIGN-UNDECLARED-CAPABILITY FIRES. This is the sharp no-union proof: if the sets unioned, the outer `network` would cover the inner foreign and the lint would stay silent. CODE UPDATED S356 r4: the co-occurring Nominal refusal was `E-FOREIGN-SIDECAR-NOMINAL` (fired at the `use foreign:` site); that code is RETIRED and the refusal now fires once at the nested-`<program>` DECLARATION as `E-NESTED-PROGRAM-CONTEXT-NOMINAL`. REGRESSION PIN: in S356 r3 BOTH codes fired on this file, and it still passed 894/894 because neither was listed in `notCodes`. The retired code is now pinned absent.
rationale: §23.5.4: a nested `capabilities=` REPLACES the ancestor's set for its subtree (mirrors §23.2.1 `lang=`); it does NOT union. The inner explicit `[]` governs the inner foreign → empty set → the §23.5.5 presence-nudge fires. E-NESTED-PROGRAM-CONTEXT-NOMINAL co-occurs (the §4.12.5 sidecar runtime is Nominal, refused at its declaration per §4.12.3/§4.12.9). E-FOREIGN-010 does NOT fire: `svc` resolves against the `<program name="svc">` the `use foreign:svc` sits inside. No E-SCOPE-001, no E-FOREIGN-CAPABILITY-UNKNOWN. COVERAGE NOTE: the harness contract is set-based, so it cannot express "fires exactly once"; the cardinality half is pinned by `compiler/tests/integration/nested-program-sidecar-unclaimed.test.js`.
